resale_co.name: Residential Reoccupancy Inspection (Residential Resale Inspection); Certificate of Inspection
resale_co.issued_by: Waterford Township (form posted by the Construction & Zoning Enforcement office; the Township code lists it as a fire prevention smoke and CO inspection fee)
resale_co.lead_time: Apply at least 10 days before settlement for the lowest fee
requirements: Smoke alarm on each floor including the basement and within 10 feet of a bedroom
Battery smoke alarms must be 10-year sealed; hardwired (110 volt) alarms cannot be replaced with battery alarms
Smoke alarms less than 10 years old (or per manufacturer replacement date)
Carbon monoxide alarm within 10 feet of a bedroom, less than 5 years old (or per manufacturer)
House number visible from the street, 3 to 6 inches tall
Passed water and septic certifications must be submitted before the certificate is released
A house with a cesspool cannot be sold until a septic system is installed; if a new system is needed, show money in escrow
Secondary power (meter and electrical panels) and all utilities on and working (listed on the 2025 form)
Do not take Township trash and recycling carts and do not leave trash at the curb

fees.label: Inspection, applied 4 to 9 days before settlement
Inspection, applied 2 to 3 days before settlement

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Residential Reoccupancy Inspection form (settlement date, block, lot, lock box code and location, owner, buyer and realtor contacts) and submit it to Waterford Township, 2131 Auburn Ave, Atco, NJ 08004. Pay by cash, check or money order. Include passed water and septic certifications.
resale_co.contact_title: Fire Official (DCA fire directory); the Township form gives no named contact

evidence.quote: ***PASSED WATER AND SEPTIC CERTIFICATIONS MUST BE SUBMITTED BEFORE WE RELEASE CO***
Any house that currently has a cess pool cannot be sold until a septic system is installed.
*FIRE CERTIFICATE IS ONLY GOOD FOR 30 DAYS*

Smoke detector and CO detector inspections. Smoke detector inspections to be conducted on all one- and two-family residential dwellings for resale, change of occupancy, and annual inspection for rental units.

resale_co.notes: Waterford uses one combined Residential Reoccupancy / Resale Inspection. Township Code section 124-7A(7) (read on ecode360; section 124-7 last amended 8-13-2025 by Ord. No. 2025-11) sets it as a smoke detector and CO detector inspection fee of $75 (ten days or more), $125 (four to nine days) and $200 (two to three days), matching the form, so the code fee is not listed again. The form adds Township items (water and septic certifications, cesspool rule, house number) and calls the result a 'Certificate of Inspection' and the 'CO'. The same fee covers the fire certificate; pay once. The tiers say 'days prior', not business days. The form lists a 'No Show / No Answer at Door' charge with no amount. An older 2025 version (NEW-CO.pdf) with the same fees and the ext. 307 phone is still online. Township Code Chapter 137 Article II (1977) also makes the seller responsible for smoke detectors on any sale. Landlord registration is a separate rental program.

requirements: Smoke alarms less than 10 years old (or per manufacturer replacement date)
Carbon monoxide alarms less than 5 years old (or per manufacturer replacement date)
Battery smoke alarms must be 10-year sealed; hardwired alarms cannot be swapped for battery units

authorities.name: Waterford Township Fire Prevention (municipal local enforcing agency, Fire Official Craig Fallstick)
authorities.lead_time: Apply at least 10 days before settlement for the lowest fee; certificate good for 30 days

fees.label: Same combined reoccupancy inspection fee (pay once), applied 10 days before settlement
Same combined reoccupancy inspection fee (pay once), applied 4 to 9 days before settlement
Same combined reoccupancy inspection fee (pay once), applied 2 to 3 days before settlement

authorities.how_to_apply: Use the Township Residential Reoccupancy Inspection form; the smoke and CO alarm certificate is issued from that inspection.

evidence.quote: A Certificate of Inspection will only be issued when the premises meet the minimum requirements of the New Jersey State Uniform Fire Code, N.J.A.C. 5:70-4:19.
The transferor of any dwelling unit is responsible for installation of said detection devices.

Berlin Borough is the LEA for Waterford Township. AS OF APRIL2025 NO LONGER A SHARED SERVICE

fire_cert.notes: The DCA directory lists Waterford's fire code enforcing agency as municipal, with smoke detector compliance handled by 'Waterford Twp Fire Prev' and Fire Official Craig Fallstick. The July 2026 LEA registry says the old Berlin Borough shared service ended in April 2025, although the directory entry still mentions an 'SSA with Berlin Boro'. Waterford is not on the DCA state smoke cert list. The Construction page lists a Township Fire Inspector and fire inspection hours (Mon and Wed, 3 to 6 pm), but does not say which office staffs the reoccupancy inspection. The form does not mention a portable fire extinguisher, which the 2025 state law (P.L.2025, c.19) dropped from the sale certificate.

other_items.label: Water and septic certifications
other_items.detail: Passed water and septic certifications must be submitted before the Township releases the certificate (mark public water, private well, public sewer or septic).

other_items.label: Cesspool replacement
other_items.detail: A house with a cesspool cannot be sold until a septic system is installed; if a new system is needed, proof of escrowed funds is required.
